title: Task, async, await, and ValueTask (the Task-based Asynchronous Pattern)
hook: async is not a runtime daemon. The C# compiler rewrites your method into a state machine that parks on await and resumes when a Task or ValueTask completes.

blocks.text: The Task-based Asynchronous Pattern (TAP) is C#'s model for async I/O. An async method returns quickly with a Task (or ValueTask) representing the rest of the work. At each await, if the awaited operation is already complete, execution continues synchronously. If not, the compiler-generated state machine captures locals, hooks a continuation, and returns. When I/O completes, the continuation runs the next state. This is why you can write linear code for Redis, then HTTP, then a message publish.

entries.plainDefinition: The .NET convention: async methods return Task or ValueTask; callers await them.
A reference type representing an asynchronous operation. Can be incomplete, completed, faulted, or canceled.
A struct awaitable that can hold a result, a Task, or an IValueTaskSource. Avoids Task allocation on sync-complete paths.
entries.example: return cachedValue; // completes synchronously, no Task heap object.

entries.plainDefinition: Compiler-generated code that stores locals and resumes at the correct point after each await.
entries.example: Locals that look like stack variables may live on a heap box during awaits.

blocks.text: Understanding the compiler transformation explains why async methods can allocate, why ValueTask exists, and why you should not use async on methods that never await. Task is the default return type with a rich API: WhenAll, WhenAny, and exception aggregation. ValueTask is an allocation optimization for paths that usually finish synchronously — like a memory cache hit. Never await the same ValueTask twice; the underlying source may have been reused.

blocks.title: ValueTask rule of thumb
blocks.body: Use Task for public APIs unless a profiler shows Task allocations on a path that usually completes synchronously. Await a ValueTask at most once, then forget it.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Call the async method
items.body: The method starts executing synchronously until the first await.

items.title: Hit an await
items.body: If the awaited Task is complete, continue inline. If not, capture state and return the Task to the caller.

items.title: I/O completes
items.body: A continuation is scheduled on the thread pool (or SynchronizationContext).

items.title: Resume
items.body: The state machine restores locals and continues from the next statement after await.

diagram.title: async method state machine
diagram.source:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Running
  Running --> AwaitCheck: hit await
  AwaitCheck --> Running: Task already complete
  AwaitCheck --> Suspended: Task incomplete
  Suspended --> Running: continuation fires
  Running --> [*]: method returns

snippet.label: Hot cache path with ValueTask
snippet.explanation: A memory hit completes without allocating a Task. A Redis miss still awaits. Callers must await the ValueTask at most once.

snippet.label: Valid async return types
snippet.explanation: The compiler cares about the async modifier and return type. The Async suffix on method names is convention, not a compiler rule.

snippet.label: Task.Run vs async — different purposes
snippet.explanation: Task.Run offloads CPU work to another pool thread. async composes I/O waits. Confusing them is a common interview trap.

blocks.title: async functions in C# vs JavaScript
rows: Every async function allocates a Promise
Continuations may run on different pool threads
Microtasks always on the same JS thread

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Awaiting the same ValueTask instance twice after a cache miss that used IValueTaskSource. Using async on a method that never awaits — the compiler warns, and you still pay a state machine. Confusing Task.Run (queue CPU work) with async (compose waits). Returning ValueTask from a public API without measuring whether the allocation matters.

interviewTakeaways: await is a compiler transformation, not a new thread.
ValueTask is an allocation optimization for completed-sync paths; await it once.
Public surface area should usually return Task unless you have measured otherwise.

jsTsCorrelations.concept: async functions always return a Promise
jsTsCorrelations.note: A JS async function boxes a Promise even on a sync return. C# can return ValueTask to skip a heap object on the sync path; JS has no equivalent struct awaitable.
